scenes.headline: How a model builds a screen by only choosing
scenes.sub: json-render plus Jev: your code offers options, the model picks keys.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Fudge! This model builds whole screens without writing a single token of interface. Here's how.

scenes.text: Instead of emitting a component tree, a decision model picks from options your code enumerated. Code does the assembling.
scenes.mark: picks from options your code enumerated
scenes.say: The idea: the model never writes the interface. It picks from options your code enumerated.

scenes.title: Write the screen, or choose it

left.title: A generating model
items: Emits markup or a component tree
Can name components you don't have
Needs a validator and a repair pass
left.say: A generating model writes the tree. It can name components you don't have, so it needs a repair pass.

right.title: A decision model
items: Props and actions come from your recipes
right.say: A decision model only returns keys you offered. Props come from your own recipes, so nothing needs repair.

steps.say: You write the candidates: fully configured elements, with props, state and actions. The playground has forty-two.
The composer turns them into multiple-choice questions. Jev sees an id and a description, never the props.

steps.note: the Gateway lists Jev's maximum output tokens as 0
steps.say: Jev answers with keys it was offered. Its maximum output is listed as zero tokens.
The composer copies each chosen recipe into the spec, and your registry renders it.

items.say: Round one asks which elements the screen needs, one question per group of rival candidates.

items.text: Round two: where does each go?
items.say: Round two asks each element's parent slot and its place among siblings.
Parallel answers can still form a cycle, so the whole tree is checked before publishing.

scenes.label: evaluation calls for an eight-element dashboard, not one per element
scenes.say: On the docs' dashboard prompt: eight elements, two calls. The count doesn't grow with the screen.

scenes.label: per candidate, added to every request: the catalog rides along
scenes.note: a 32,000 context window fits on the order of 200 recipes
scenes.say: The cost moved into the request. Every candidate adds six hundred sixty-eight point six bytes, every call. So the context window caps your catalog.

scenes.text: When the model only chooses, components, props and actions are yours by construction. You pay by enumerating them.

recap: Jev picks keys your code enumerated
The whole catalog rides every request
scenes.say: To recap: the model picks keys, two rounds build the screen, and the catalog rides every call.
